v.rationale: The two implementations are nearly identical in structure: the same form requests, a ProductSort enum, #[Scope] scopes, withQueryString, to_route()->with() flash redirects, an x-layouts.app layout with inline CSS, and well-covered Pest suites that pass (37 and 38 tests). The probes broke the tie. impl-1 does not escape LIKE wildcards (q=% returns every product) and never shows filter validation errors on the index, so users are silently redirected. impl-2 escapes wildcards (with a test), shows filter errors, uses the hidden-0 checkbox idiom with @checked(old()), and has more reusable field/select components with @props, $attributes and @error. impl-1 has its own pluses: Model::shouldBeStrict(), a slot-based field wrapper, and an x-price component. Against it is an @include partial that misuses @props. impl-2's weaknesses are a redundant getRouteKeyName alongside {product:slug} and currency formatting on the model. Both share a design flaw: strict validation of public GET filters can redirect to itself when the referrer is the same invalid URL. Overall impl-2 is narrowly better.
